mainTopic: Combining סכך פסול and אויר, and the two versions of the dispute between רב and שמואל on how much סכך פסול disqualifies
overview: The amud opens as רבה finishes telling how the students of רב asked whether a little סכך פסול and a little אויר add up to make a סוכה invalid. רבה says each one is a separate fixed measure (שיעור), four טפחים versus three. Because the measures are different, they do not combine. Under the students' view, where the problem is the gap (הפלגה) from the wall, they should combine. אביי objects that in a small סוכה the measures seem equal. רבה answers that a small סוכה fails only because too little valid roofing is left. The גמרא then challenges רבה's rule from fabrics of different sizes that combine for טומאה. It answers that the fabrics share a common size of a טפח, since each can serve as a patch on a donkey's saddle. Next comes the נהרדעא version of the dispute between רב and שמואל about סכך פסול in the middle versus along the side. The גמרא tests both versions against a משנה about a wide board and a ברייתא about sheets and boards combining. The amud ends by bringing a ברייתא about cedar boards, to be examined on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה: the rule depends on fixed measures, so different measures do not combine
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains his own view. Invalid roofing and empty space each disqualify a סוכה only at their own fixed size. Since the two sizes are not the same, a small amount of each cannot be added together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ruling depends on whether something reaches the required measure or does not. Here, neither one reaches its measure. Since their measures are not equal to each other, they do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his reply to the students of רב. He explains why, in his view, a little סכך פסול plus a little אויר does not make the סוכה invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, 'four טפחים of סכך פסול' and 'three טפחים of אויר' are two separate, fixed measuring rules. Each works only when its own measure is reached. Because one measure is three and the other is four, there is no single shared measure for them to add up to, so they stay separate.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed legal measure or size
It does not reach the required measure
Their measures are equal
To each other
They combine; they add up together

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of רבה's sentence, which started on the previous part of the daf. The phrase 'משום שיעורא ולאו שיעורא הוא' means 'it is a question of whether it reaches the measure or not.' It does not mean 'it is not because of a measure.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the foundation of רבה's position. Combining two disqualifications requires them to share the same measure. That idea is exactly what אביי will challenge in step 3.

phrases.english: It is because of [whether it is] the measure or not the measure.
phrases.notes: This continues רבה's sentence on the previous amud: 'According to me, who holds the rule is about measure.'

phrases.english: This [case] is not the measure,
phrases.notes: Neither the invalid roofing nor the empty space reaches its own measure.

phrases.english: since their measures are not equal to each other —
phrases.notes: Empty space disqualifies at three טפחים, and invalid roofing at four.

phrases.english: they do not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's answer to the students of רב earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the 'שיעור' approach, סכך פסול and אויר do not combine, because their measures (four versus three טפחים) are different.

steps.title: רבה: under the students' gap-based view, the two should combine
steps.stepSummary: רבה tells the students of רב that under their own view, the combination should work. In their view, invalid roofing disqualifies because it creates a gap (הפלגה). A gap is a gap, whether it is made of invalid roofing alone or of invalid roofing plus empty space.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to you, who say the measure is because of separation: what difference does it make to me whether it was separated by invalid roofing, or separated by invalid roofing and empty space?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה contrasts his view with the view of the students of רב. He shows that under their reasoning, invalid roofing and empty space should add up together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the real problem with four טפחים of סכך פסול is the distance it puts between the wall and the valid roofing, then the material filling the gap does not matter. Invalid roofing plus empty space makes the same gap. So under the הפלגה view, combining is logical. Under רבה's measure view, it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you (plural)
Separation or gap; distancing the valid roofing from the wall
What difference does it make to me
Invalid roofing material
Empty space or gap in the roof

steps.whatToRemember: The two views lead to opposite results. If the rule is about fixed measures (רבה), they do not combine. If the rule is about a gap (הפלגה, the students of רב), they should combine.

phrases.english: But according to you, who say
phrases.notes: Addressed to the students of רב.

phrases.english: [that] the measure is because of separation —
what difference is it to me if it was separated by invalid roofing,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי אִתַּפְלַג בִּסְכָךְ פָּסוּל וַאֲוִיר.
phrases.english: what difference is it to me if it was separated by invalid roofing and empty space.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the other side's reasoning against רבה's own view from step 1, completing his account of the exchange.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the הפלגה view, סכך פסול and אויר should combine, since a gap is a gap no matter what fills it.

steps.title: אביי: in a small סוכה the measures are equal
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה. Even if the measures differ in a large סוכה, in a small סוכה three טפחים of invalid roofing also disqualifies. So the measures there are equal, and they should combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And according to the Master too, granted that their measures are not equal in a large סוכה. In a small סוכה, are their measures not equal?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's reason from step 1. He points to a case where the two measures seem to be the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a minimum-size סוכה (seven by seven טפחים), three טפחים of סכך פסול also makes it invalid. That is the same number as for empty space. If רבה's only reason against combining is that the measures differ, then in a small סוכה they should combine.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the Master (you) as well
Granted; even if we accept
A large סוכה
A small, minimum-size סוכה
Is it not? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And according to the Master too,

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דְּלָא שָׁווּ שִׁיעוּרַיְיהוּ בְּסוּכָּה גְּדוֹלָה,
phrases.english: granted that their measures are not equal in a large sukkah,

phrases.aramaic: בְּסוּכָּה קְטַנָּה מִי לָא שָׁווּ שִׁיעוּרַיְיהוּ?
phrases.english: in a small sukkah, are their measures not equal?
phrases.notes: In a seven-by-seven סוכה, three טפחים of invalid roofing also disqualifies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבה gave in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that סכך פסול and אויר never combine because their measures are not equal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a small סוכה, three טפחים of סכך פסול disqualifies, just like three טפחים of אויר. So the measures are equal there, and by רבה's own logic they should combine.

steps.title: רבה: the small סוכה fails for lack of minimum size, not equal measures
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that in a small סוכה, three טפחים of invalid roofing does not disqualify because it has a shared measure with empty space. The סוכה is invalid because not enough valid area is left to meet the minimum size of a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it is not because their measures are equal to each other. Rather, it is because the סוכה lacks the measure of a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his position. He explains that the small-סוכה case runs on a different reason entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three טפחים of סכך פסול in a seven-by-seven סוכה leaves less than seven טפחים of valid roofing. The minimum size is then missing. So the invalid roofing itself never really became a three-טפח disqualification. The measures were never truly equal, and רבה's rule from step 1 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that case)
It is not there; it is missing
The minimum required size of a סוכה (seven by seven טפחים)

steps.whatToRemember: A small סוכה becomes invalid with three טפחים of סכך פסול only because its minimum valid size is gone. This does not mean invalid roofing has a three-טפח measure. So רבה's rule holds: the different measures do not combine.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that סכך פסול disqualifies at three טפחים. Its measure stays four. The small סוכה fails for a completely separate reason: it is too small.

phrases.english: He said to him: There, it is not because
their measures are equal to each other,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵיתֵיהּ לְשִׁיעוּרָא דְסוּכָּה הוּא.
phrases.english: rather, it is because the measure of a sukkah is lacking.
phrases.notes: Fewer than seven טפחים of valid roofing remain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּשָׁווּ שִׁיעוּרַיְיהוּ לַהֲדָדֵי הוּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the reason: the small-סוכה case is explained by a different law (the minimum size of a סוכה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In a small סוכה, סכך פסול disqualifies at three טפחים, so its measure equals that of אויר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The small סוכה is invalid only because less than the minimum סוכה size remains. The measure of סכך פסול itself is still different from that of אויר, so they do not combine.

steps.title: Different materials with different sizes do combine for impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה's rule that things with unequal sizes never combine. It cites a משנה that gives four different minimum sizes for garment, sackcloth, leather and matting, and a ברייתא that says these materials combine with each other anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that wherever two things have different sizes, they do not combine? But we learned in a משנה: a garment is three by three, sackcloth is four by four, leather is five by five, and a mat is six by six. And a ברייתא taught on it: garment with sackcloth, sackcloth with leather, and leather with mat all combine with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's rule that items with different sizes can never be added together. It brings a case where items with different sizes clearly do combine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each material has its own minimum size before it can become impure through מדרס of a זב. Still, the ברייתא says a piece of garment joined to a piece of sackcloth, and so on, combine to make up the size. So 'unequal sizes' does not automatically block combining, and this seems to contradict רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their measures or required sizes
They combine or join together to make up a size
A woven garment or cloth
Sackcloth, usually made of goats' hair
Animal hide or leather
A woven mat, usually of reeds

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is not about סוכה at all. It is about טומאה of fabrics, the impurity a זב gives to things he sits or treads on (מדרס). The גמרא borrows it only to test רבה's general rule about combining different sizes.

phrases.english: And anywhere that they are not equal
phrases.notes: Restating רבה's principle in order to question it.

phrases.english: their measures to each other, do they not combine?
phrases.notes: This is phrased as a question, but it's really a challenge.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: the garment, three by three,
phrases.notes: That's three טפחים by three, the smallest size that can get טומאת מדרס.

phrases.english: the sackcloth, four by four,
the hide, five by five,
a mat, six by six.
phrases.notes: The משנה lists four materials, each with its own size.

phrases.english: And it was taught on it: the garment and the sackcloth,
phrases.notes: A ברייתא commenting on the משנה.

phrases.english: the sackcloth and the hide, the hide and the mat —
combine with one another.
phrases.notes: They combine even though their sizes are not equal, which seems to contradict רבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּלָא שָׁווּ שִׁיעוּרַיְיהוּ לַהֲדָדֵי לָא מִצְטָרְפִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה's answer to אביי, the גמרא challenges the underlying principle of רבה's view from a different area of הלכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle that items with unequal disqualifying sizes cannot combine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows materials with unequal minimum sizes combining for טומאה, so unequal sizes cannot be a reason by itself to block combining.

steps.title: The fabrics combine because they share a one-handbreadth size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the fabrics combine for a specific reason given by רבי שמעון. All of them can become impure as a seat, since at the size of a טפח by a טפח any of them can serve as a patch. That shared size lets them combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is as the reason is taught. רבי שמעון said: What is the reason? Because they are all fit to become impure as a seat. As we learned: one who cuts out a piece of any of them, a טפח by a טפח, it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by explaining that the fabric case is different. Those materials have a common size where they are all treated the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every one of these materials, when cut to a טפח by a טפח, can become impure as a patch for a seat. Since there is one size where they are all equal, they can combine in other areas too. סכך פסול and אויר have no such shared size, so רבה's rule still stands for סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is fit or suitable
To become impure as a seat (impurity of a זב's sitting place)
One who cuts or trims a piece into shape
A handbreadth by a handbreadth

steps.whyThisMatters: It sharpens רבה's principle. What matters is not whether the sizes differ in one context, but whether the two things share any common size at all. A shared size makes them combinable.

phrases.english: There, it is as the reason is taught,
phrases.notes: The fabric case has its own explicit reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason —
since it is fit to become impure as a seat.
phrases.notes: All the materials can serve as patches for a seat.

phrases.english: As we learned: one who trims from any of them
phrases.notes: A supporting משנה.

phrases.english: a handbreadth by a handbreadth — it is impure.
phrases.notes: This is the shared size that is the same for all the materials.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by showing why the fabric case is different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): the fabrics have a shared size, while סכך פסול and אויר do not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Materials with different sizes can always combine, which would undermine רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Materials combine only when they share some common size. The fabrics share the size of a טפח, so they combine, while סכך פסול and אויר remain separate.

steps.title: What is a tiny one-handbreadth piece good for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what use a piece only a טפח by a טפח could have. An item only becomes impure if it is useful for something.
steps.simpleTranslation: A handbreadth by a handbreadth, what is it fit for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask a clarifying question about the answer it just gave. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that has no use cannot become impure. So the גמרא needs to know what practical use a tiny scrap could have. Without such a use, the shared size of a טפח would not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: For what is it fit or useful?

phrases.english: A handbreadth by a handbreadth — for what is it fit?
phrases.notes: A small scrap seems useless, and useless things cannot become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the practical basis of the shared size of a טפח cited in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical use makes a piece the size of a טפח capable of becoming impure.

steps.title: It can serve as a patch on a donkey's saddle
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, in the name of רבי ינאי, answers that a piece a טפח by a טפח is useful as a patch on a donkey's saddle. That use is enough for it to become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי ינאי: Since it is fit to place on a donkey's back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving a real use for the small piece. That use is patching a donkey's saddle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey's saddle is a kind of seat, so a patch for it can become impure as a seat. This confirms that all the fabrics share a meaningful size of a טפח. The fabric case is therefore truly different from סוכה, and רבה's view survives the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: On the back of a donkey, meaning on its saddle
In the name of (quoting an earlier sage)

steps.whatToRemember: Things with different sizes can combine only if they share some common size. The fabrics all share the size of a טפח, since each can serve as a patch on a donkey's saddle, so they combine. סכך פסול and אויר share no such size, so according to רבה they do not combine.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
Since it is fit (to place it)
on the back of the donkey.
phrases.notes: It can serve as a patch on the donkey's saddle, which is a kind of seat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 7 and completes the defense of רבה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A piece the size of a טפח is useful as a patch for a donkey's saddle, so it can become impure as a seat.

steps.title: The נהרדעא version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The previous version of the dispute was how they taught it in סורא. In נהרדעא they taught it differently: שמואל says invalid roofing disqualifies at four טפחים in the middle and four אמות on the side, and רב says four אמות everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they say this teaching in the way we just learned. In נהרדעא they teach it like this: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: invalid roofing in the middle of the סוכה disqualifies it at four טפחים. Along the side, it disqualifies it only at four אמות. And רב said: whether along the side or in the middle, it disqualifies only at four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us there is a second version of the same argument, taught in a different city. In this version the names and the rulings shift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סורא version, רב was the one who split the rule: four טפחים in the middle and four אמות on the side. In the נהרדעא version, that split rule belongs to שמואל, and רב holds a single rule of four אמות everywhere. From here on, the גמרא will test both versions against older sources.

keyTerms.meaning: A major Babylonian city and yeshiva, the home of רב
Another major Babylonian city and yeshiva, the home of שמואל
Version or wording of a teaching
Invalid roofing material on a סוכה
Four cubits, a much larger measure than four טפחים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In סורא, רב holds 'four טפחים in the middle.' In נהרדעא, that same view belongs to שמואל, and רב holds 'four אמות everywhere.'
steps.whyThisMatters: Both coming challenges depend on knowing which version you are working with, so keep both versions clearly in mind.

phrases.english: In Sura they say this teaching
phrases.notes: Refers to the version already learned earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: in this version.
In Neharde'a they taught it as follows:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Invalid roofing in the middle disqualifies with four handbreadths.
Along the side, it disqualifies with four cubits.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אָמַר: בֵּין מִן הַצַּד בֵּין בָּאֶמְצַע
phrases.english: And Rav said: whether along the side or in the middle
it disqualifies with four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a second version of the רב and שמואל dispute discussed earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the נהרדעא version, שמואל says middle disqualifies at four טפחים and side at four אמות. רב says four אמות in both places.

steps.title: A משנה about a wide board challenges שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a סוכה with a board four טפחים wide on top is valid. That fits רב, who requires four אמות, but it seems to contradict שמואל, who says four טפחים in the middle disqualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: if someone placed a board four טפחים wide on top of the סוכה, it is valid. This works well for רב, who said that both in the middle and along the side the measure is four אמות. That is why the סוכה is valid. But according to שמואל, who said four טפחים in the middle disqualifies, why is it valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה and uses it to attack שמואל's opinion in the נהרדעא version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A board four טפחים wide is invalid roofing, and it reaches exactly four טפחים. For רב that is not enough to disqualify, since he needs four אמות. For שמואל, four טפחים in the middle should disqualify, yet the משנה says the סוכה is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A board or plank
Valid
It works well (for one view), introducing a contrast
Why?

phrases.english: We learned: if he placed a board on it
that is four handbreadths wide, it is valid.
It works well for Rav, who said

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בָּאֶמְצַע בֵּין מִן הַצַּד בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: whether in the middle or along the side, it is four cubits,
that is why it is valid.
But according to Shmuel, who said in the middle it is four handbreadths,
why is it valid?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: נָתַן עָלֶיהָ נֶסֶר שֶׁהוּא רָחָב אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests שמואל's view from the נהרדעא version against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that four טפחים of invalid roofing in the middle disqualifies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה validates a סוכה with a four-טפחים invalid board, which should disqualify it according to שמואל.

steps.title: The board was placed along the side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a board placed along the side, where even שמואל requires four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A board placed along the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by limiting the משנה to a specific case: the board is along the side, not in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל agrees that along the side only four אמות disqualifies. So a four-טפחים board on the side does not disqualify, and the משנה fits his view. If the board were in the middle, שמואל would say the סוכה is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowing answer)
Along the side (near the wall)

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
A board along the side.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers to a board along the side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to validate a four-טפחים board anywhere, including the middle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers only to a board along the side, where שמואל also requires four אמות.

steps.title: A ברייתא about sheets and boards combining
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: two sheets combine to disqualify, two boards do not, and רבי מאיר says boards are like sheets. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: two sheets combine. Two boards do not combine. רבי מאיר says: boards are like sheets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It is setting up the next move, where this source will be tested against the two versions of רב's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sheets spread on the סוכה are invalid roofing, and two of them add together toward the disqualifying measure. The תנא קמא says boards do not add together this way, and רבי מאיר says they do. The key question will be: combine to reach what measure?

keyTerms.meaning: Sheets (cloth)
Boards
They combine (to reach a measure)

phrases.english: Come and hear: two sheets combine.
Two boards do not combine.
Rabbi Meir says: boards are like sheets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to test the two versions of רב's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The סורא version of רב's opinion, in which four טפחים of סכך פסול in the middle disqualifies. The ברייתא is set up here and turned against that version in step 13. The נהרדעא version fits the ברייתא easily.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ברייתא's word 'combine' will be shown to make sense in only one version.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits one version of רב but not the other
steps.stepSummary: In the נהרדעא version, 'combine' means the pieces add up to four אמות. In the סורא version, where רב said four טפחים in the middle, the ברייתא is hard to explain. Boards that are four טפחים each do not need to combine, and narrower boards are just like reeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the version in which רב said that whether in the middle or along the side the measure is four אמות. What does 'combine' mean? They combine to make four אמות. But for the version in which רב said four טפחים in the middle, what is the case? If each board has four טפחים, why do they need to combine? If each board does not have four טפחים, they are just ordinary reeds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא makes sense in the נהרדעא version of רב, and then raises a sharp question against the סורא version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a measure of four אמות, two boards can each be too small alone but reach four אמות together, so 'combine' makes sense. With a measure of four טפחים, a board four טפחים wide already disqualifies alone, so combining is pointless. A board narrower than four טפחים counts like a plain reed, which is valid roofing, so why should רבי מאיר let it combine to disqualify?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How would this look?
If this... if that (a two-sided dilemma)
To combine
Mere reeds (ordinary valid roofing)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Four' without a unit in the סורא version means four טפחים, not four אמות. The whole question depends on that small measure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dilemma threatens the סורא version of רב, and the next part of the גמרא will need to resolve it.

phrases.english: It works well according to that version

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב בֵּין בָּאֶמְצַע בֵּין מִן הַצַּד בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: in which Rav said that whether in the middle or along the side, it is four cubits,
phrases.notes: This is the נהרדעא version.

phrases.english: what does 'combine' mean?
They combine to make four cubits.
But according to this version
in which Rav said that in the middle it is four handbreadths,
phrases.notes: This is the סורא version.

phrases.english: what is the case?
If they each have four handbreadths,
why do they need to combine?
If they do not have four handbreadths,
they are merely reeds!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְהָךְ לִישָּׁנָא דְּאָמַר רַב בָּאֶמְצַע בְּאַרְבָּעָה הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 12 to challenge the סורא version of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The סורא version, in which רב said four טפחים of invalid roofing in the middle disqualifies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: boards of four טפחים each need no combining, and narrower boards count as valid reeds, so the ברייתא's 'combine' has no case to fit.

steps.title: The boards are four טפחים wide and combine to four אמות on the side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא is talking about boards that are each four טפחים wide. 'Combine' means they join together to make four אמות along the side of the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the case is where the boards are four טפחים wide. What does 'combine' mean? They combine to make four אמות along the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13. It shows how the ברייתא can work even in the סורא version of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that four-טפח boards should not need to combine, because in the middle each one already disqualifies by itself. The answer is that the ברייתא is talking about boards along the side, where you need four אמות, so the boards must add up. This reading works for both the סורא version and the נהרדעא version.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. It keeps the original case and explains it differently.
Along the side, next to the wall of the סוכה
Four אמות. This is the amount of invalid roofing that disqualifies along the side.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two measures. Four טפחים is the width of each board. Four אמות is the total that the boards add up to along the side.

phrases.english: Really, it is where they have four (טפחים) each,
and what does 'combine' mean?
They combine to make four אמות along the side.
phrases.notes: Along the side, the measure is four אמות even according to the stricter view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 13 against the סורא version of רב
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case and the word 'combine'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Combine' meant that narrow boards add up to four טפחים in the middle, which would make no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The boards are four טפחים each and add up to four אמות along the side, so the ברייתא fits both versions.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about roofing with cedar boards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about cedar boards. If the boards are four טפחים wide, everyone agrees the סוכה is invalid. If they are narrower, רבי מאיר invalidates it and רבי יהודה validates it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone roofed a סוכה with cedar boards that are four טפחים wide, everyone agrees it is invalid. If they are not four טפחים wide, רבי מאיר says it is invalid and רבי יהודה says it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to test the opinions about wide boards. This is a setup. The גמרא will next show what this source proves or challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא adds an important fact: the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה is only about boards narrower than four טפחים. For boards of four טפחים, everyone agrees the סוכה is invalid. The גמרא will use this point to check the positions of רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Cedar boards
Everyone agrees
Rules it invalid
Rules it valid

steps.whyThisMatters: It narrows the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה to narrow boards only. Wide boards are invalid according to everyone.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If one roofed it with cedar boards
that are four (טפחים) wide,
everyone agrees it is invalid.
If they are not four (טפחים) wide,
רבי מאיר rules it invalid
and רבי יהודה rules it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the challenge, the גמרא brings another ברייתא about wide boards to test the views again
steps.kashyaTarget: The versions of רב and שמואל about how much invalid roofing disqualifies a סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says boards of four טפחים are invalid according to everyone. The גמרא will examine how this fits each version of the dispute.
